tagline: Off the caldera's edge, the Henrys Fork drops twice.
intro: Idaho 47 leaves Ashton as Main Street, runs east through Marysville and bends north past Warm River into the Caribou-Targhee National Forest. At the old Bear Gulch ski area, 12.4 miles out, Forest Route 294 takes over and carries on to US 20.
The Henrys Fork comes down off the Island Park caldera here and goes over both Mesa Falls on the way. They are the only major falls in Idaho not used for irrigation or power.
season: Visit Idaho calls spring through fall great by car. Winter is for those with snowmobiles or cross-country skis.

moments.title: Warm River
moments.text: Warm River, population four at the 2020 census, incorporated in the 1940s so that its little resort could hold a liquor license.

moments.title: Lower Mesa Falls
moments.text: Below the Grandview overlook, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s, the river squeezes between basalt columns and drops 65 feet.

moments.title: Upper Mesa Falls
moments.text: The river pours 114 feet over volcanic ash 1.3 million years old, beside a log building the Mesa Power Company put up in the 1910s, later an inn and now the visitor center.

practical: In winter Forest Route 294 is closed to cars and becomes a snowmobile route.
